summary: The candidate follows from the supplied accepted facts. Pooling counts every positive atlas label once at each of its two distinct opposite endpoints, while the edge-capacity constraints and reservoir degree formula give the claimed per-fiber mass bound. The pooled metronoid barycenters yield one atom per physical base, so their fiber-depth bounds sum over distinct fibers to genuine ambient halfspace domination. The hard inequality then gives the atom-size, endpoint-count, residual-rank, and affine-dimension screens with the stated strict constants. For every same-parity affine basis and nontrivial partition, the saturated subspace lattices give integral coordinates and an injective full-rank product-simplex chart; its product vertices are distinct integral midpoint fibers. Scaling the pooled endpoint densities to the pairwise minimum masses and applying positive-root metronoid convexity produces the required actual vertex points. The rank-one minorant satisfies the generic factorized lattice-polysimplex theorem's product-root hypothesis, and its factor energies, including all simplex vertices, give exactly the lower bounds in (23) and (25). Boundary, zero-rank, and no-frame cases are covered.
